texts.preamble: The State Of Maharashtra Through Food ... vs Pankaj Gupta, Nominee, Adani Wilmar ... on 12 February, 2019 Author: Ravindra V. Ghuge Bench: Ravindra V. Ghuge *1* 908ao9o19 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Appeal From Order
texts.arguments: Under Section 68, the Adjudicating Officer, who is to be designated by the State Government and who is not to be below the rank of the Additional District Magistrate of the district, is vested with the powers of the civil court and all proceedings before him shall be deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of Sections *2* 908ao9o19 193 and 228 of the Indian Penal Code. It is also provided that it would be deemed to be a court for the purposes of Sections 345 and 346 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 3 Proviso below Section 69(3) indicates that no offence, for which punishment of imprisonment has been prescribed under this Act, shall be compounded. 4 The learned AGP has specifically relied upon the judgment of the Allahabad High Court in the matter of Pradeep Kumar Gupta vs. State of U.P., 2015 (3) ACR 2924 : 2015 (6) ADJ 351 : 2016 Cri.L.J. 122, wherein, it has been concluded that an appeal under Section 70(1) of the 2006 Act, against the decision of the adjudicating officer under Section 68, before the Food Safe Appellate Tribunal would be treated as a Civil Miscellaneous Appeal and not a criminal appeal. 5 The learned Advocate for the Respondents submits that he would cause research on this aspect in order to look up to judicial pronouncements of this Court or the Honourable Supreme Court, if any.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 5 The learned Advocate for the Respondents submits that he would cause research on this aspect in order to look up to judicial pronouncements of this Court or the Honourable Supreme Court, if any.

It is also provided that it would be deemed to be a court for the purposes of Sections 345 and 346 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 3 Proviso below Section 69(3) indicates that no offence, for which punishment of imprisonment has been prescribed under this Act, shall be compounded. 4 The learned AGP has specifically relied upon the judgment of the Allahabad High Court in the matter of Pradeep Kumar Gupta vs. State of U.P., 2015 (3) ACR 2924 : 2015 (6) ADJ 351 : 2016 Cri.L.J. 122, wherein, it has been concluded that an appeal under Section 70(1) of the 2006 Act, against the decision of the adjudicating officer under Section 68, before the Food Safe Appellate Tribunal would be treated as a Civil Miscellaneous Appeal and not a criminal appeal.
